sentences.en: Picture the land around any given interstate exit, the massive concrete overpasses, the bow-tie loop-de-loops of on-and-off ramps.
sentences.zh: 想象一下任何一个州际公路出口周围的土地，庞大的混凝土立交桥，以及上下匝道的蝶形盘桥。

sentences.en: In California, the agency that maintains the land around our highways is the California Department of Transportation, or Caltrans.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州，负责维护高速公路周边土地的机构是加州交通局，简称 Caltrans。

sentences.en: In 2017, Caltrans counted 7,000 homeless encampments next to California roads.
sentences.zh: 2017年，加州交通局统计出加州道路旁有 7000 个无家可归者营地。

sentences.en: Okay, now zoom in on one of these encampments.
sentences.zh: 好，现在把镜头拉近，看看其中一个营地。

sentences.en: In Berkeley, California, off of Interstate 80 at the university exit.
sentences.zh: 在加利福尼亚州伯克利市，位于 80 号州际公路大学出口附近。

sentences.en: There are about 70 people living there, scattered around in tents and makeshift structures.
sentences.zh: 那里大约住了 70 人，分散在帐篷和简易棚里。

sentences.en: For years now, Caltrans has been posting notices for the people camped at this exit to vacate.
sentences.zh: 多年来，加州交通局一直向这个出口的露宿者张贴限期搬迁通知。

sentences.en: And every couple weeks, they attempt to enforce the notices by coming in with police and cleaning crews and confiscating any belongings people can't pack up and move in time.
sentences.zh: 每隔几周，他们就会出动警察和清洁队来强制执行通知，没收人们来不及收拾和搬走的任何随身物品。

sentences.en: And it's always incredibly stressful for the people who live there.
sentences.zh: 对住在那里的人来说，这总是压力极大。

sentences.en: We've got to break down his house.
Can you move that out of the way?
He doesn't need to move it out of the way.
He needs to get his house.
And then, after the police and Caltrans maintenance crews leave,
sentences.zh: 然后，在警察和加州交通局的维护人员离开后，

sentences.en: the homeless campers take the belongings they've salvaged and move right back to the same spots they were in before.
sentences.zh: 无家可归的露宿者们拿回他们抢救出来的物品，又搬回了原先呆的同一个地方。

sentences.en: A couple weeks later, Caltrans comes again, over and over, rinse and repeat.
sentences.zh: 几周后，加州交通局又来了，一次又一次，周而复始。

sentences.en: One of the people living in this encampment in Berkeley is Kate Cody, who goes by her initials, KC.
sentences.zh: 伯克利这个营地的居民之一是凯特·科迪，大家按她的首字母叫她 KC。

sentences.en: I met KC last year in October, when it was starting to get chilly.
sentences.zh: 我去年十月见到 KC 时，天气开始变凉了。

sentences.en: The listeners don't know, this is a very misty and cold day.
sentences.zh: 听众们不知道，这是一个非常多雾且寒冷的日子。

sentences.en: KC has long silver hair, so bright it almost looks like platinum blonde.
sentences.zh: KC 有着一头长长的银发，亮得几乎像铂金色。

sentences.en: And narrow, kind of mischievous eyes.
sentences.zh: 还有狭长、带点顽皮的眼睛。

sentences.en: You could mistake her for a hippie, but she's surlier than moSt.
sentences.zh: 你可能会把她误认为嬉皮士，但她比大多数人都要难相处。

sentences.en: She'll read any book she can get her hands on.
sentences.zh: 她会阅读她能拿到手的任何一本书。

sentences.en: I really can't go to sleep without them.
sentences.zh: 我真的离了它们就睡不着觉。

sentences.en: Now I've gotten well past the point where I fall asleep with a book on my nose and break my glasses.
sentences.zh: 现在我已经习惯了把书顶在鼻子上睡觉然后把眼镜压碎的情况。

sentences.en: The last time Caltrans came through for a sweep of the encampment, a bunch of KC's belongings were thrown into a dump truck.
sentences.zh: 上一次加州交通局来清理营地时，KC 的许多东西都被扔进了自卸卡车。

sentences.en: But she saved some precious iteMs.
sentences.zh: 但她抢救出了一些珍贵的物品。

sentences.en: And when you lost all your stuff from when Caltrans, did they get books or...?
sentences.zh: 当加州交通局拿走你所有东西时，他们拿走了书还是……？

sentences.en: They were buried in with beads.
She saved her books and her beads.
sentences.zh: 她保住了她的书和珠子。

sentences.en: KC makes beaded jewelry that she sells in an Etsy store.
sentences.zh: KC 制作串珠首饰，并在 Etsy 网店上出售。

sentences.en: But Caltrans threw away her tent and her bed.
sentences.zh: 但加州交通局扔掉了她的帐篷和床。

sentences.en: For a couple weeks after that, she slept under a cast-aside boat sail.
sentences.zh: 在那之后的几周里，她睡在一块被丢弃的船帆下面。

sentences.en: Now she has a new tent, which she's set up on the shoulder of the off-ramp, right next to the stop sign.
sentences.zh: 现在她有了新帐篷，搭在下匝道的路肩上，紧挨着停车标志。

sentences.en: And she'd like to be left alone.
Do you think that the city should...
Like, that anyone has a right to camp if they don't have...
sentences.zh: 比如，如果没有……任何人都有权露营吗？

sentences.en: No, but all we want to know is, we don't want to break the law.
sentences.zh: 不，但我们只想知道，我们不想违法。

sentences.en: We have to live someplace and have to sleep on face.
sentences.zh: 我们总得找个地方住，总得睡在什么地方。

sentences.en: Just like, I need to live.
And what were KC's options, besides living in a tent next to the highway?
sentences.zh: 除了住在高速公路旁的帐篷里，KC 还有什么选择？

sentences.en: She seemed to feel that renting her own apartment in Berkeley was completely out of reach.
sentences.zh: 她似乎觉得在伯克利租一套属于自己的公寓简直遥不可及。

sentences.en: You know, they're renting not apartments, not bedrooms, beds for $1,200 a month near the college.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在大学附近，他们租的不是公寓，不是卧室，而是每月 1200 美元的床位。

sentences.en: KC had about $900 a month coming in through Social Security.
sentences.zh: KC 通过社会保障金每月大约有 900 美元的收入。

sentences.en: And it did seem unlikely, given her age, 66, and the fact that she can only walk very slowly using a walker,
sentences.zh: 考虑到她 66 岁的年龄，以及她只能靠助行器非常缓慢地行走这一事实，

sentences.en: that she was going to be able to get a job to increase her income.
sentences.zh: 她似乎不太可能找到一份工作来增加收入。

sentences.en: She tried staying in shelters, but hated the lack of privacy.
sentences.zh: 她尝试过去收容所住，但讨厌那里毫无隐私可言。

sentences.en: I cannot handle that at all.
Plus, most shelters don't allow pets.
sentences.zh: 另外，大多数收容所不允许带宠物。

sentences.en: And KC has a scraggly little black-and-white dog named Eva, who rarely leaves her side.
sentences.zh: KC 有一只瘦骨嶙峋的黑白相间的小狗叫伊娃，几乎形影不离地跟着她。

sentences.en: But there was still another option.
sentences.zh: 但其实还有另一个选择。

sentences.en: KC has a son named Lonnie, who lives in the mountains of Colorado.
sentences.zh: KC 有个儿子叫朗尼，住在科罗拉多州的群山中。

sentences.en: The two of them were estranged for most of their lives,
sentences.zh: 他们母子俩大半生都处于疏远状态，

sentences.en: for complicated reasons that I don't fully understand.
sentences.zh: 原因很复杂，我不是完全理解。

sentences.en: But about five years ago, they reunited, and they really care about each other.
sentences.zh: 但大约五年前，他们团聚了，而且他们真的很关爱彼此。

sentences.en: Lonnie doesn't have much money either, but he told his mom,
sentences.zh: 朗尼也没什么钱，但他对妈妈说，

sentences.en: move here to my town and I'll help you.
sentences.zh: 搬到我这里来，我会帮你的。

sentences.en: We'll get you a place, and you can stay at my house until you find your own.
sentences.zh: 我们会给你找个地方，在你找到自己的住处之前，你可以住在我家。

sentences.en: But so far, KC hasn't taken Lonnie up on his offer to come live in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 但到目前为止，KC 并没有接受朗尼让她去科罗拉多居住的提议。

sentences.en: I'm not playing about hating the cold.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌寒冷可不是开玩笑的。

sentences.en: If I never see a snowflake again in my life, I'll be so happy.
sentences.zh: 如果我这辈子再也见不到一片雪花，我都会高兴得不得了。

sentences.en: I think a lot of people would be surprised that he wouldn't take...
sentences.zh: 我想很多人会惊讶她居然不肯接受……

sentences.en: Should I take advantage of him?
We were forced apart for a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 我正在慢慢重新建立联系，好吗？

sentences.en: And if I moved to a very small town in Colorado,
sentences.zh: 如果我搬到一个科罗拉多州非常小的城镇，

sentences.en: We don't know each other well enough yet.
KC told me that she thought of Lonnie as an escape hatch.
sentences.zh: KC 告诉我，她把朗尼视为一条逃生舱口。

sentences.en: But if she wouldn't use her escape hatch to escape the constant sweeps by Caltrans,
sentences.zh: 但如果她不愿利用她的逃生舱口来逃避加州交通局不断的清扫，

sentences.en: or the difficulty of living 10 feet from a busy interstate off-ramp,
sentences.zh: 或者逃避住在繁忙的州际公路下匝道 10 英尺外的艰难，

sentences.en: it was hard for me to imagine when she would use it.
sentences.zh: 我很难想象她会在什么时候使用它。

sentences.en: You said he's an escape hatch,
sentences.zh: 你说他是一条逃生舱口，

sentences.en: and so I was trying to figure out the situation in which you might use your escape hatch.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在琢磨你可能会使用逃生舱口的情况。

sentences.en: You just like knowing it's there?
sentences.zh: 你只是喜欢知道他在那儿？

sentences.en: When Casey and I had this conversation,
sentences.zh: 当凯茜和我进行这次对话时，

sentences.en: I didn't think anyone would live in a tent by an interstate if they had another option.
sentences.zh: 我原以为如果有别的选择，没人会住在州际公路旁的帐篷里。

sentences.en: But it's more complicated than that.
What I came to believe is that, in general, people are where they are,
sentences.zh: 我渐渐相信的是，总的来说，人们身处他们所在的地方，

sentences.en: not necessarily because they literally have no other choice,
sentences.zh: 不一定是因为他们真的别无选择，

sentences.en: although for some that is the case,
sentences.zh: 尽管对某些人来说确实如此，

sentences.en: but because like any human making a decision,
sentences.zh: 而是因为像任何做决定的普通人一样，

sentences.en: and a tent by the side of the road seemed the least bad.
sentences.zh: 而路边的帐篷似乎是其中最不坏的一个。

sentences.en: I think it's why you do occasionally hear people say,
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么你偶尔会听到有人说，

sentences.en: I chose to be out here,
which, by the way, you do hear sometimes.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你有时确实会听到这种话。

sentences.en: I believe what people mean is,
I chose this off a short list of lousy options.
sentences.zh: 我在一份糟糕的选择清单中选择了这个。

sentences.en: But there's still agency in that,
sentences.zh: 但这其中仍然包含自主权，
而自主权是极其宝贵的。

sentences.en: the encampment was the best of the lousy options,
sentences.zh: 这个营地是那些糟糕选择中最好的一个，

sentences.en: for reasons I was just beginning to understand.
sentences.zh: 原因我才刚刚开始理解。

sentences.en: what the camp provided to her was so important
sentences.zh: 这个营地提供给她的东西是如此重要，

sentences.en: that even when she was found to be vulnerable enough
sentences.zh: 以至于即使当人们发现她足够脆弱、

sentences.en: to make it to the top of the list
and be offered a new way out,
sentences.zh: 并获得一条新的出路时，

sentences.en: it would be hard for her to accept it.
This is According to Need, Chapter 5.
sentences.zh: 这里是“按需分配”，第 5 章。

sentences.en: Casey is kind of a tough guy,
but it's a toughness that covers up a lot of trauma.
sentences.zh: 但这坚强之下掩盖了许多心灵创伤。

sentences.en: I get, I get, I cry about everything.
sentences.zh: 我，我，我为什么事都会哭。

sentences.en: I just, I feel very bad
because then it's like, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为这就好像是，你知道的，

sentences.en: Casey grew up in New Jersey
and ran away from home as a teenager,
leaving behind a mother that she says was abusive.
sentences.zh: 抛下了她所说虐待过她的母亲。

sentences.en: I ruined my mother's life because I was born,
sentences.zh: 因为我的出生，我毁了我母亲的一生，

sentences.en: But mostly she just can't talk about her mom at all.
sentences.zh: 但大多数时候她根本绝口不提她妈妈。

sentences.en: As a young adult, Casey made her way out to California.
sentences.zh: 成年后不久，凯茜来到了加利福尼亚。
她过过一段艰难的生活。

sentences.en: She spent some time in prison.
sentences.zh: 她在监狱里呆过一段时间。

sentences.en: although she hasn't used in seven years.
sentences.zh: 尽管她已经七年没碰过了。

sentences.en: And all I have to do is three days in a row.
sentences.zh: 而我只需要连着做三天。
在她生命的大部分时间里，

sentences.en: Casey had steady housing and income
sentences.zh: 凯西都有稳定的住所和收入，
但她对非传统的生活方式

sentences.en: And to some degree, she's welcomed them.
sentences.zh: 而且在某种程度上，她很欢迎这种生活。

sentences.en: She's lived in warehouses and school buses.
she lived in a community of people

sentences.zh: 人们在一处旧垃圾填埋场上

sentences.en: on top of an old landfill

sentences.zh: 不过，别把这想象成垃圾堆。

sentences.en: There were some chunks of concrete
sentences.zh: 周围散落着一些混凝土块

sentences.en: but this landfill had mostly been covered over
sentences.zh: 但这个垃圾填埋场大部分都长满了

sentences.en: you could watch the sun setting
Casey was kind of a queen bee

sentences.zh: 垃圾填埋场居民中的“蜂王”，
她的邻居们都很尊敬她，

sentences.en: and she felt like she had a role there.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己在那里扮演着一个角色。

sentences.en: I found a film from that time on YouTube.
sentences.zh: 我在YouTube上找到了那段时期的视频。

sentences.en: but Casey looks so much younger and healthier.
sentences.zh: 但凯西看起来年轻健康得多。

sentences.en: Her cheeks are plump and rosy,
as she cooks a big meal for everyone
I had taken the chicken breast fillets,
and I serve them with a white gravy and salad.
sentences.zh: 配上白肉汁和沙拉端上桌。

sentences.en: she was making food for a birthday party
sentences.zh: 她正在为他们举办的生日派对准备食物，

sentences.en: one of the landfill's many dogs.
sentences.zh: 垃圾填埋场众多狗狗中的一只。

sentences.en: forced the landfillians to leave in 2014,
sentences.zh: 于2014年强迫垃圾填埋场的居民离开后，

sentences.en: the land was turned into a park
sentences.zh: 这片土地变成了一个公园，
也就是湾区居民所熟知的

sentences.en: And Casey moved into a broken-down RV,
sentences.zh: 凯西搬进了一辆破旧的房车，

sentences.en: where she stayed a few years.
But eventually she had to leave there too,
sentences.zh: 但最终她也不得不离开那里，

sentences.en: which is when she moved to the encampment
sentences.zh: 也就是在那时，她搬到了
伯克利80号州际公路旁的营地，

sentences.en: Some of her old friends from the landfill
sentences.zh: 她的一些垃圾填埋场的老朋友

sentences.en: The landfill loomed so large in Casey's mind
sentences.zh: 垃圾填埋场在凯西心中占据着如此巨大的分量，

sentences.en: even though she was in a considerably
part of her was still there,
sentences.zh: 但她的一部分仍然留在那儿，

sentences.en: or still looking for what she had there.
sentences.zh: 或者仍在寻找她在那里拥有的一切。

sentences.en: But where that place had been quiet
now Casey lived five feet from a stop sign,
sentences.zh: 如今凯西却住在离停车标志只有五英尺远的地方，

sentences.en: that the drivers could easily see inside.
sentences.zh: 以至于司机们能轻而易举地看到里面。

sentences.en: And the spot was prone to flooding
it's cold and damp and raining,
sentences.zh: 天气又冷又潮湿还下着雨，

sentences.en: and Casey is sick inside of her tent.
sentences.zh: 凯西生病了，躺在帐篷里。

sentences.en: is trying to make sure Casey's tent
sentences.zh: 正试图确保凯西的帐篷

sentences.en: doesn't flood from all the rain.
Sarah's tent is up on wooden pallets
sentences.zh: 萨拉的帐篷搭在木托盘上，

sentences.en: so that the water can drain under it.
sentences.zh: 这样水就能从下面排走。

sentences.en: Why is it draining through the tent?
sentences.zh: 为什么水会流进帐篷里？

sentences.en: Are you trying to get the water to flow?
sentences.zh: 你是在想办法把水引走吗？

sentences.en: Last year when it was raining,

sentences.zh: 我是说，字面意义上的湖。
她也需要人帮忙弄木托盘。

sentences.en: Her mobility just isn't good enough
sentences.zh: 她的行动能力根本不足以

sentences.en: to do this kind of chore on her own.
So she relies on people like Sarah for help.
sentences.zh: 所以她依靠像萨拉这样的人来帮忙。
我的手指都没有知觉了。

sentences.en: Sarah goes inside of her tent
to talk to her boyfriend, Zach.
and she's sick and also needs water,
sentences.zh: 而且她生病了，还需要水，

sentences.en: And you need to go get it.
And he's not interested in helping right now.
sentences.zh: 他现在对帮忙一点兴趣也没有。

sentences.en: just admit that you're just a douchebag.
sentences.zh: 爽快承认你就是个混蛋吧。
你真是一点礼貌都没有。

sentences.en: Now you won't help Casey get water.
sentences.zh: 现在你都不肯帮凯西弄点水。

sentences.en: You want me to do it,
as I'm digging a ditch to save her tent.
sentences.zh: 而我正在挖沟来保护她的帐篷。

sentences.en: Sarah and Zach continue to fight,
that's it, she's had it with the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 够了，她对这一切彻底忍无可忍了。

sentences.en: She doesn't finish digging the ditch,
doesn't go get Casey pallets or water,
sentences.zh: 也没有去给凯西拿木托盘或水，

sentences.en: she just goes to another part of the encampment,
sentences.zh: 她只是去了营地的另一个地方，

sentences.en: I thought a lot about this interaction afterwards,
sentences.zh: 事后我久久地思考着这次互动，

sentences.en: how a normal, everyday thing for most of us,
sentences.zh: 思考着对我们大多数人来说再寻常不过的事，

sentences.en: can turn into a crisis in the camp.
sentences.zh: 怎么就会在营地里演变成一场危机。

sentences.en: It means that everyone is stressed all the time,
sentences.zh: 这意味着每个人随时都处于压力之中，

sentences.en: and sometimes even people with good intentions,
sentences.zh: 有时甚至连心怀善意的人，

sentences.en: to do what needs to be done.

sentences.zh: 研究人员实际上已经研究过这一点，

sentences.en: erode our ability to make good decisions
sentences.zh: 如何侵蚀我们做出明智决定

sentences.en: Still, eventually someone will get Casey water.
sentences.zh: 不过，总会有人给凯西送水。
凯西的一切都要依赖邻居

sentences.en: Neighbors run to the store for her
sentences.zh: 邻居会帮她跑腿去商店买东西，

sentences.en: Her friend Sid cleans her tent for her.
sentences.zh: 她的朋友西德帮她清理帐篷。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's just friends being friends.
sentences.zh: 有时只是朋友之间的守望相助。

sentences.en: Other times she barters with people.
sentences.zh: 其他时候她会跟别人进行物物交换。

sentences.en: It's hard for Casey to get rid of her own garbage,

sentences.zh: 凯西自己很难处理垃圾。

sentences.en: The guy who comes to pick up my recycling
sentences.zh: 有个来收我回收垃圾的家伙，
